messages.subject: Hierarchical Gaussian Process Regression
parts:
Hi,

Similar to a previous post on grouped splines (https://groups.google.com/g/r-inla-discussion-group/c/W4nTB8h1ZAY/m/31D3FaTpAgAJ), I am looking to fit non-linear relationships as a 1D Gaussian Process regression. However, I would also like to fit this in a hierarchical format where there is a population-level 1D Gaussian Process, which is accompanied by varying effects by individual that is a zero-mean 1D Gaussian Process.

So far, I have been able to technically fit a model that includes a 1D SPDE model on each covariate in addition to another smooth term of the same covariate that uses "groups". However, I'm unsure how to connect these two terms to achieve the hierarchical model I'm looking for. Here is a simple example demonstrating the formula for how I'm attempting to fit the model:

formula <-  y ~ -1 + Intercept +
  f(log.bathym.pop, model = spde.list[[1]]) +
  f(log.bathym.id, model = spde.list[[1]], group = log.bathym.id.group,
    control.group = list(model = 'iid')) +
  f(id1, model = "iid", hyper = list(theta = list(initial = log(1e-6), fixed = TRUE)))

While I understand how to specify random effects when using simple linear terms for a regression, it's unclear to me how to do this when specifying A matrices as needed for the 1D SPDE model. Any suggestions or advice on how to fit this as a hierarchical model are welcome.

Best,
   Josh

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Hierarchical Gaussian Process Regression
parts:
I’d recommend looking into the inlabru package interface, that removes all the A matrix and inla.stack code from the user side of things, so specifying the predictor connections becomes much easier.
If you do need an actual A matrix, you can use the same method as used internally by inlabru, with a bru_mapper_multi() with one mapper for main and and another for the group part of the model. See the component specification and mapper systems vignettes, available under Articles on the inlabru GitHub.io site.

Finn
